units.text: EXT. VILLAGE PIER, TUG-OF-WAR - SUNSET
A rope as thick as a man's wrist lies across the weathered planks of a fishing pier, its centre marked with a red rag.
Below, the tide slaps the pilings.
A crowd of villagers presses along the railings, quiet.
SAOIRSE KEANE, forty, anchor of the harbour team, wraps the rope twice round her forearm and plants her boots against a plank she has used for twenty years.
Opposite her, FINBARR MCGRATH, her cousin and rival, spits on his palms and rubs them together, grinning like a man who has already won.
Behind him the rest of his team braces.
At the rail, old DONAL, the referee, lifts a handkerchief, and beside him NUALA, thirteen, Saoirse's daughter, grips the rail so hard her knuckles whiten.
Take the strain!
units.name: DONAL

units.text: Saoirse leans back.
Finbarr leans back.
The red rag does not move.
A gull settles on a piling to watch.
Still got your mother's hands, Saoirse.
units.name: FINBARR

units.text: And you've still got her mouth.
units.name: SAOIRSE

units.text: The rope groans.
A plank cracks under Finbarr's heel and the rag slides a foot toward the harbour side.
Nuala shrieks.
Saoirse digs in, the cords of her neck standing out, her boots skating on salt-slick wood.
Mam, don't let go!
units.name: NUALA

units.text: Let go, Saoirse! Let go before you're hurt!
units.name: FINBARR

units.text: Not this year, Fin.
units.name: SAOIRSE

units.text: The rag crosses the line.
Finbarr's team stumbles.
Then the old rope, frayed through twenty summers, parts with a gunshot crack, and both teams go down in a tangle of limbs and oilskin, Saoirse across her cousin's chest, and the pier erupts.
No contest!
units.name: DONAL

units.text: Mam!
units.name: NUALA
